title.narrative: 4th Global Summit of the Strong Cities Network in New York City on 19-21 September 2023

description.narrative: The summit will convene mayors and other local government leaders, as well as city-level practitioners and civil society actors from more than 70 cities around the globe. It will showcase the unique contributions those actors have made and can make in preventing and responding to violent extremism and the democratic backsliding that a growing number of communities are facing. Throughout the summit, emphasis will be placed on the importance of ensuring that all city-led efforts in this area are non-discriminatory and, more broadly, promote human rights. Danish support will allow local leaders and representatives from ODA-eligible countries to participate in the summit. Their participation is likely to increase their knowledge on how city-led efforts may prevent and respond to violent extremism, build resilience and enhance social cohesion. Their participation also enables engagement with relevant UN bodies that are engaged in preventing and countering violent extremism (P/CVE) to elevate the voices of local leaders and the perspectives of local authorities in the UN’s P/CVE efforts.

title.narrative: An expected outcome of the engagement is increased capacity and motivation of cities and local leaders in ODA-eligible countries to develop, implement and sustain multi-stakeholder, multi-disciplinary approaches to preventing hate, extremism and polarisation.

An outcome indicator is therefore familiarity (on a rating scale) reported by participants with multi-stakeholder, multi-disciplinary approaches and practices for prevention discussed at the Strong Cities Global Summit (disaggregated by participant type).

target.value: An increase in familiarity with approaches and practices of more than 2 out of 5 on a 5-point rating scale, equating to a mean average rating of better than 'slightly familiar'.

actual.value: 3.93 out of 5.00 on a 5-point rating scale, equating to a mean average rating of better than 'very familiar'. This translates to a 27%. increase in familiarity with multi-stakeholder, multi-disciplinary approaches and practices for prevention.

title.narrative: An expected output of the engagement is that city representatives from ODA-eligible countries are provided with an opportunity to connect and exchange knowledge, approaches and good practices with global counterparts and prevention stakeholders at the “4th Global Summit of the Strong Cities Network”.

An output indicator is relevance and usefulness (on a rating scale) reported by participants of multi-stakeholder, multi-disciplinary approaches and practices for prevention discussed at the Summit (disaggregated by participant type).

target.value: 3 out out of 5 on a 5-point rating scale, equating to a median average rating of 'moderately relevant and useful'.

actual.value: 4 out of 5 on a 5-point rating scale, equating to a median average rating of 'very relevant and useful'.

title.narrative: An expected output of the engagement is support provided to city representatives from ODA-eligible countries to participate in the Strong Cities Global Summit.
